facts.claim: Relative motion of grains during avalanches is linked to dune sound; synchronization is an influential explanation.
facts.sensitivity: Clapping is an original analogy, not an observed microscopic experiment. Motion shown slow, not at audible frequency.

facts.claim: Suitable singing-dune sand produced sound in laboratory avalanches in a hard-bottom channel.
facts.sensitivity: Only under tested conditions; do not claim ordinary sand can always sing.

facts.claim: Sorting the mixed-size sand into a narrower grain-size range produced a more defined note.
facts.sensitivity: Sieve selects existing grains; it does not resize them. No numerical spectrum claimed.

facts.claim: Field studies proposed layered-dune waveguides, while other experiments emphasize flowing grains.
facts.sensitivity: Competing interpretations; no claim of complete resolution.
